Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer whose AI agent calls tools in the app. On 2026-10-31 Kenneth's own Bambu P1S failed to connect through the printer chat because the app had found the printer in cloud mode, hid that from the model, and refused with "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now"; the model then guessed. That case was fixed on `claude/festive-lederberg-693438` (status tool reports search state and a `seen` list with reasons; connect refusals state the facts; a note reaches the model when the first printer appears or after 15 s; a held UDP port 2021 is reported), and one approved live Sonnet chat against the real printer then told the person the truth. A read-only sweep afterwards found 11 more places where tools drop what the app saw, and a second agent confirmed them, five by live reproduction without a model. Kenneth asked why so many exist despite the MCP tool guide; the answer he did not dispute is that the guide governs the model's side while these bugs are on the app's side, for the four causes named in the brief. His standing rules: no fix for a failure not reproduced in the real app; live-model runs cost money and need his approval per batch; a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description; the standing prompt holds principles only; small, additive changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files; rare failures may keep a generic error; temporary notes stay untracked and are never hidden from `git status`.

Task:
Address the class of bug where a JusPrin tool returns a generic, false or empty result while the app knew more, as a method and a guard rather than as eleven separate fixes. Kenneth's words: "address these issues in a more systematic manner, instead of case by case."

Start from the two untracked reports. The sweep is `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/printer-live-p1s/tool-silent-failures-sweep-2026-11-01.md` (11 findings, all from reading the code, with per-finding reproduction recipes). The independent check is `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/tool-silent-failures-sweep-check-2026-11-01.md`: all 11 hold on reading, and findings 4, 7, 8, 9 and 11 were reproduced live with no model through the shell harness's `--manual-mcp` mode (recipe in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe.md`). Read both before anything else; they are reports, not instructions, so verify what you rely on. Make your own worktree from `5f3bd2e59a` on `claude/printer-live-p1s` (that is `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the Bambu connection fix `ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501` and a live-chat scenario). Never build or edit in `.claude/worktrees/printer-live-p1s` or `.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438`; other sessions own them.

The question the method must answer, for every tool: does every state the app can distinguish at the moment it answers map to a result the model can distinguish? The four causes found so far, which your inventory should confirm or correct: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` reports a failed Bambu connection as "the selected printer changed"; a Moonraker or OctoPrint test's error text is reduced to a bool); (2) filters encode product decisions and drop the reason (connection candidates, hidden presets, printers without an access code); (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined (`Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp` never sends `ConnectStatusFailed`; the "selected printer changed" harness check simulates a selection change, not a failure); (4) Kenneth's 2026-10-15 rule that rare failures get one generic error was applied to common, distinguishable states.

Deliver, each in its own commit on your branch:
1. An inventory, as a tracked document under `agent-docs/jusprin/`, listing per tool the states the app can tell apart when it answers and the result each one produces today, marking every collapse. Cover the tools in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp` and the printer-chat tools in `PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`.
2. A contract rule, written where the existing tool error contract lives (the one code list in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp` and the guide that explains it): a reason travels with every refusal and every empty result; sibling tools share one failure shape; a generic error is allowed only for failures that are rare and that the app itself cannot distinguish. Say in the rule how it relates to the 2026-10-15 rule rather than silently replacing it.
3. A guard: tests that enumerate the states per tool (Catch2 under `tests/agent/`, and harness checks where a tool needs the real panel), plus fakes able to produce every failure the real plug-in or host can report, starting with `ConnectStatusFailed` with a code in the Bambu fake and error bodies in a Moonraker or OctoPrint stand-in. Each guard test must fail on the current code before its fix and pass after; show both.
4. Fixes only for findings you reproduce first in the real app or the real harness, never only against a fake you just taught to fail; say for each finding which it was. A finding you cannot reproduce stays open in the inventory with what you tried. Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files stay small and additive, with the rebase notes `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` requires.

Constraints: no live-model runs at all; Kenneth's real P1S at 192.168.0.198 stays in cloud mode with LAN Only off, and before any harness run against it `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` must print nothing; isolated `--datadir` always, never another running JusPrin; builds with `-j4` after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -l ninja`, one build per directory, never restarted to change targets; delete only your own harness data directory by its printed path. Working notes stay untracked at your worktree root. Nothing merged or pushed. Done means the inventory and rule are committed, the guard tests exist and were shown failing first, the reproduced findings are fixed with agent tests, AgentUI tests and the `--printer-setup` harness green, and your final report says in plain English which findings were reproduced, fixed, or left open and why.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_05f541e9-abc1-4ee8-a987-a295f5fa2c65
I'll start by reading the two sweep reports and the shared notes folder, then make my own worktree from the named commit.

Inventory tool states and collapses per tool
Write contract rule in ToolErrors.hpp and guide
Teach fakes every failure the plug-in reports
Write guard tests, show them failing first
Reproduce findings in real app or harness
Fix reproduced findings, make guards pass
Run agent, AgentUI and printer-setup harness

# Tools that withhold what the app saw: findings to confirm

Written 2026-11-01 for an agent who has not seen the session that produced it. Please try to prove each finding wrong. Every finding comes from reading the code. **Nothing here has been run or reproduced, and nothing has been fixed.**

## The question

JusPrin is a desktop 3D-printing slicer forked from OrcaSlicer. An AI model chats with people and calls tools in the app. On 2026-10-31 a printer connection failed because the app had found the printer in cloud mode, hid it from the model, and refused with "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now". That bug is fixed on this branch.

Kenneth, the product owner, then asked: do other tools have the same problem, where a refusal or an empty result fails to carry what the app saw? This report is the answer. Kenneth has not approved any fix.

A finding qualifies when both of these hold:
1. The app knew something more specific at that moment, or could have known it by reading its own state.
2. The model received a generic statement, a false statement, or an empty result that it cannot tell apart from a different situation.

A generic message does not qualify when the app itself received no reason.

## Where to look

- Branch `claude/printer-live-p1s`, commit `5f3bd2e59a`. It is `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the connection fix (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) and a test scenario. The `candidates`, `seen` and `search` code in findings 1 to 3 differs on `jusprin-newui`, which does not have the fix yet.
- This worktree also holds an uncommitted wording fix that changes sentence text only. It does not affect any finding.
- Paths below are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`.
- Make your own worktree from `5f3bd2e59a`. Do not build or edit in `.claude/worktrees/printer-live-p1s`, and never touch `.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438`.

## Rules for confirming

- Do not fix anything. Report only.
- No live-model runs: they cost money and Kenneth approves them batch by batch. None of these checks needs a model.
- Do not change Kenneth's real P1S (192.168.0.198). It stays in cloud mode with LAN Only off. Before any harness run against it, `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` must print nothing, and `route -n get default` must show the Mac on the printer's 192.168.0.x network.
- Do not drive another running JusPrin. Use an isolated `--datadir`.
- Builds: check `uptime` and `pgrep -l ninja` first, use `-j4`, one build per directory, and never restart a build to change targets.
- Delete only your own harness data directory, by its printed path, never the `jusprin-shell-*` glob. Failed runs can leave API keys there.
- Temporary test edits and your notes stay uncommitted.
- A failure against a fake is weaker evidence than one against the real app or printer. Say which one you used.

## How to run the tools without a model

For findings 4 to 11, tools on MCP can be called directly. Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`, then use `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()`. It takes about 20 s per run. The full recipe and two traps are in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe.md`. One trap matters here: `slice_start` on an already sliced, unchanged plate has hung before.

The printer tools are not on MCP. For findings 1 to 3, use `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (the Bambu checks around line 5620) or `PrinterSetup` directly. `Testing/README.md` explains the Bambu fake.

---

## Serious: the model is told something false

### Finding 1: a failed Bambu LAN connection is reported with an unrelated reason

**What the app sees.** `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:2092-2105`. The plug-in reports `ConnectStatusFailed` with a code. The handler clears the selected printer (line 2096). For code `"5"` it erases the saved access code (lines 2099-2100) and shows the person "Incorrect password". For other codes it shows "Connect %s failed! [SN:%s, code=%s]". This handler is upstream OrcaSlicer: its commits `45bf4a99f1eb`, `e17c8bfb8009` and `d20656b8698e` are on `upstream/main`.

**What JusPrin does with it.** `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:493-524` never sees the failure or its code. It only sees what the handler left behind. These lines are fork code: `8334b3395ba` and `9f739dccf24` are on no upstream branch.

- **Code `"5"`, wrong access code.** Clearing the code makes `has_access_right()` false (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.hpp:191`). `get_my_machine_list()` then omits the printer (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:663-673`), so `machine` at line 493 is null. The check at line 508 needs `machine != nullptr` and is skipped. Line 516 gives **"The printer is no longer available. Refresh the printer list and try again."**
- **Any other failure code, or `ConnectStatusLost`.** The code is kept, so `machine` is not null, but the selection is empty. Line 508 is true, and line 510 gives **"The selected printer changed. Select this printer again to reconnect."**

Either sentence reaches the model as "Connection to X failed: ..." (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:720-721`). The real reason never does. The access code being erased is also not reported.

**Existing test.** `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:5634-5637` checks the sentence, but it simulates a person changing the selection with `set_selected_machine("")`. It cannot tell that case from a failed connection.

**How to check.** `Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp` only ever sends `ConnectStatusOk` and `ConnectStatusLost` (lines 637, 655), so it needs a temporary change to send `connect_fn(ConnectStatusFailed, id, "5")`, and again with another code. Read `backend->connection(name)` afterwards. The real-printer version needs LAN Only on and a deliberately wrong code, so only Kenneth can do it.

**What would disprove it.** The attempt ends some other way first, or the machine stays in the list after a wrong code. I also have not confirmed that the real plug-in sends `"5"`; that comes from reading the handler.

### Finding 2: a Moonraker or OctoPrint test's real answer is thrown away

**What the app sees.** `src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp:77-82` fills `msg` from `format_error`, for example "HTTP 401: ...", a timeout, or an unresolvable host name (`src/slic3r/Utils/PrintHost.cpp:115`). Lines 92-97 also catch a host that answers but isn't Moonraker: "The host responded but it doesn't look like Moonraker". `src/slic3r/Utils/OctoPrint.cpp:160-163` does the same on error. Both are upstream code.

**What JusPrin does with it.** `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:625-626` declares `detail`, passes it to `host->test(detail)`, and keeps only true or false. Line 647 always says **"Could not reach the print host. Check its address, API key and network, then try again."** That is false when the host was reached and rejected the key, or when it is a different kind of service.

**How to check.** Run a small local HTTP server and call `connect_host(name, "moonraker", "127.0.0.1:<port>", "key")`, then read `connection(name).message` until it stops saying connecting. Try three cases: 401 on `/server/info`, 200 with `{}`, and the server stopped. I predict the same sentence all three times, while the log shows different errors.

**For whoever fixes it later.** `format_error` includes the response body, and some messages are translated, so the text would need bounding before the model reads it.

### Finding 3: the connection tools still hide printers they can see

**Where.** `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:481-492`. The loop drops these with no record:

| Dropped | Line | What the model is told |
|---|---|---|
| A printer of another model, such as a P1P when the person chose P1S | 482 | "found no printer of this model", which is literally true, but the likely explanation is hidden |
| A printer of the same model, when this saved printer is linked to a different one | 484 | "found no printer of this model", which is false |
| A printer of the same model already linked to another saved printer | 486-489 | "found no printer of this model", which is false |

The sentences are at `PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:479`, `481` and `776`. The tool's description says it "reports what it has found of that model so far" (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1600`), so the first row's limit is stated. The other two are not.

**How to check.** Use the fake with a second device of a different `printer_type`, then with a saved printer linked to another serial, then with two saved printers. Call `connection_status` and read `candidates`, `seen`, and the note posted after 15 s.

**A suspect I could not settle.** Line 489 also drops a printer in LAN mode whose `bind_state` isn't `"free"` (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.hpp:233`). If a real LAN-mode printer can report `occupied`, that printer would be hidden too, and it is the one kind that can be connected. Whether that happens is unknown. It needs a printer in LAN mode, or a source saying what `DevBind` reports in that mode.

---

## Medium: the model can recover, but it is misled or wastes steps

### Finding 4: `export_file` says "Slice the plate first" while a slice is running

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:330-331`. Three different states give one answer, "Slice the plate first; it has no current G-code": never sliced, last slice refused or failed, and slicing right now.

**Why it matters.** The `needs_step` code tells the model to do the named step. During a slice, `slice_start` answers "A slice is already running. Wait for it, or ask again with preempt." (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2221`). My inference, not tested: a model following this could take over a slice the person started.

**How to check.** On MCP, call `slice_start`, then immediately `export_file` with kind `gcode`. Repeat on a plate whose slice was refused.

### Finding 5: `printer_list` omits a printer the network search can hear

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2272` reads `discover_printers(true)`, which is `get_my_machine_list()` (`PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:113`). That list holds printers on the signed-in account, plus LAN-mode printers with an access code (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:651-675`). A cloud-mode printer that is announcing itself, with nobody signed in, isn't listed. This is Kenneth's P1S. The result is `items: []` with no reason, and the tool describes itself as listing "the physical printers this application knows about" (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1069`). It is available in the chats and on MCP.

**How to check.** With the printer heard (the log shows `UpdateLocalMachineInfo_WIFI`) and nobody signed in, call `printer_list`.

**Not settled.** Whether a saved Moonraker or OctoPrint printer appears. `src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp:1322` announces one under some conditions, which I did not trace.

### Finding 6: the Add chat's "On the network now" line can be wrong in both directions

**Where.** `PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:215` reads `discover_printers()` once, when the panel opens, and `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts:188-189` writes "On the network now: ...".
- **Too many:** a printer on the person's account counts if it is online through the cloud, wherever it is (`PrinterDiscovery.cpp:113-116`). It may not be on this network.
- **Too few:** a printer announcing itself without an access code, and not on the account, isn't included. `discover_nearby_printers()` (`PrinterDiscovery.cpp:123`) exists for that and is used by the add form (`PrinterConversation.cpp:913`), not by this line.
- **Empty:** the line is left out, so the model has no statement either way.

**Correction to my first version.** I implied no search had run at that point. `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:998` and `1623` start discovery when the plug-in is set up, so one may already be running. I did not settle this.

**How to check.** Open an Add chat with a cloud-mode printer heard and nobody signed in, then read the first request in the request log (`<data dir>/jusprin/request-log`). Compare it with the add form's nearby list.

### Finding 7: `slice_inspect` answers `valid: false` with no reason (new since the first list)

**Where.** `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1685-1711` and `Workspace/OrcaOutputs.cpp:233`. Its sibling `slice_report` adds `sliceFailure` when the last slice failed (`Agent/ToolResults.cpp:795-800`). `slice_inspect` doesn't, so never sliced, refused, failed and slicing right now all look alike.

**A smaller case in the same tool.** `OrcaOutputs.cpp:238-256` opens the G-code file without checking that it opened. A missing file gives `valid: true` with empty text. That is rare.

**How to check.** On MCP, call `slice_inspect` on a plate whose slice was refused, and compare with `slice_report`.

### Finding 8: `slice_report` doesn't say a slice is running

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` in `slice_report` (the comment reads "both answer no current slice"), and `Agent/ToolResults.cpp:795-800`. The description says only that an unsliced plate "says so".

**How much it matters.** When the model started the slice, `slice_start`'s note explains this. When the person started it, this tool gives no sign, though `workspace_inspect`'s slicing section does.

**Not settled.** Whether an old `sliceFailure` still shows during a new slice. I saw the failure erased at the end of a run (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935`, `950`) but did not trace the start.

**How to check.** Start a slice outside the tool, call `slice_report` while it runs, and repeat after a refused slice.

---

## Low

### Finding 9: `print_dialog_open` drops a slice failure it just looked up

**Where.** `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2105-2107`. `targets_sliced` fills `failure`, and then the message says only "This plate has no valid slice. Slice it with slice_start first".

**Why it is low (I rated this medium at first).** The model has usually been told already: the `slice-failed` skill fires on a failed slice, `workspace_inspect` includes `sliceFailure` per plate (`Agent/ToolResults.cpp:722`), and calling `slice_start` again returns the reason. The cost is a wasted step.

### Finding 10: `presets_list` doesn't count hidden presets

**Where.** `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2328`. Hidden presets are skipped, so an installed but hidden filament gives `total: 0`, the same as one that doesn't exist. The compatibility filter is stated in the tool's description, and the model can ask for all. The hidden filter can't be turned off. The description says "this installation offers", so this may be intended. Commit `09cc63eaa9` accepts a hidden preset by name when the project uses it.

### Finding 11: `settings_search` is silent when a setting is in another scope

**Where.** `Workspace/SettingsSupport.hpp:127-146` with `Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp:89`. Searching printer settings for a process setting gives `items: []` and no hint. By contrast, `settings_get` on a wrong key gives suggestions (`Workspace/OrcaSettings.hpp:24`).

---

## Withdrawn or outside the list

- **Plug-in install, withdrawn.** My first list said the model is told nothing when the installer is closed or the download fails (`PrinterConversation.cpp:253-256`). That is true, but no model turn is running at that moment, the person has seen the installer's own dialog, and the next request's instructions correctly say "Bambu's network plug-in: not installed" (`printerInstructions.ts:210-212`). Nothing false reaches the model.
- **`print_dialog_open` success, a related case.** It reports `opened: true` and "The app's send dialog is open" before the dialog opens, which happens later in a `CallAfter` (`Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2116-2124`, `Shell/ShellController.cpp`). If the plate has gone by then, the person sees a message and the model still believes the dialog opened. This is a false success rather than a refusal, and it should be rare.
- **"Choose a matching printer from the refreshed list."** `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:547` can occur if a printer vanishes while the person types the code. The app knows little more than that. Not counted.

## Reviewed and not counted

- **The reason is passed on:** `project_open` and the import tools (the app's messages travel in `report`), `slice_start` (`reason`), failed settings changes (issues with codes), `object_repair`, G-code export (the copy error), and the print-again refusals in `Shell/ShellController.cpp`. The Bambu search states are reported since `ff2fee4fbd`.
- **The app has no more to give:** 3MF export returning below 0, STL write returning false, "The app rendered nothing", and "The app did not generate the test". A calibration the person cancelled looks like that same failure, and the generator returns nothing to tell them apart.
- **Refusals that just need a fresh read:** `not_found` and `stale_workspace` say what to read again.
- **Settings hidden from reading:** I had this as unconfirmed. The seven connection keys in `kWithheldSettings` (`Workspace/SettingsSupport.hpp`) are not filtered from `settings_search` by this code path, and `settings_get` refuses them with a stated reason, so nothing is silently hidden.

## Limits of this sweep

- I read every refusal message in `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, `Workspace/*.cpp` and `PrinterSetup/`, but not every successful result.
- `object_analyze`: I read its failure handling, not each section. Empty sections there appear to be measurements, not states, but I did not check them one by one.
- `workspace_inspect`: I read the printer section, not all of it.
- I did not sweep the filament chat beyond its refusals in `PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp`, or `view_render` beyond its failure messages.
- Severity is my judgement. Rare-failure cases should be weighed against Kenneth's standing preference for a generic error on rare or speculative failures.

## Corrections since the list sent to Kenneth in chat

| In the chat list | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| #1 said a wrong access code gives "The selected printer changed" | Finding 1: a wrong code gives "The printer is no longer available"; other failures give "selected printer changed" | Erasing the code removes the printer from the list, which changes the branch taken |
| #1 "didn't check upstream or fork" | Settled: the handler is upstream, the sentences are fork | `git branch -r --contains` |
| #4 `print_dialog_open`, medium | Finding 9, low | The model has usually already been told |
| #8 implied no search had run | Finding 6, unsettled | Discovery may start with the plug-in |
| #9 plug-in install | Withdrawn | The next request states it correctly |
| Not listed | Finding 7, `slice_inspect` | Found while covering the gaps |
| Not listed | The suspect in finding 3 | I dismissed it too early: the `free` override applies only to `farm` |
| "not confirmed" on settings hidden from search | Settled, not a finding | Code path read |

The chat list's numbers map to this report as follows: 1→1, 2→2, 3→3, 4→9, 5→4, 6→8, 7→5, 8→6, 9→withdrawn, 10→10, 11→11.

## What to report back

For each finding, give one of: **confirmed**, **partly right** (say what is wrong), **wrong**, or **could not test** (say why). Include the code you read or the output you saw, whether you used a fake or the real thing, and the exact message the model received. List anything this sweep missed. Keep it in plain English and do not propose fixes unless asked.

Exit code 1
# Check of "Tools that withhold what the app saw" (2026-11-01)

Temporary note, untracked. This checks the report `tool-silent-failures-sweep-2026-11-01.md` written in the
`printer-live-p1s` worktree. Findings 1 to 3 were re-read in the code at commit `5f3bd2e59a` by me; findings 4 to 11 were
re-read by a subagent told to prove each one wrong; findings 4, 7, 8, 9 and 11 were also run against the real tools with no
model, through the shell harness in `--manual-mcp` mode (main checkout build of `69780c7af4`, whose `Workspace/`,
`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` and `ToolResults.cpp` are identical to `5f3bd2e59a`). Findings 1 to 3, 5, 6 and 10 were
not run: 1 to 3 need the Bambu fake or the printer in LAN mode, 5 and 6 need a heard printer, 10 needs a known hidden preset.

| # | Verdict | How checked | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirmed | code | `get_my_machine()` goes through `get_my_machine_list()`, which keeps a LAN printer only with an access code (`DevManager.cpp:441-449`, `663-668`), so erasing the code on failure code "5" makes `machine` null and the fork says "no longer available"; other codes clear the selection and give "selected printer changed". Whether the plug-in really sends "5" is still unverified. |
| 2 | Confirmed | code | `connect_host` passes `detail` to `host->test(detail)` and stores only pass or fail; `settle()` always says "Could not reach the print host…" (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` at `5f3bd2e59a`, lines 625-627 and 646-647). Moonraker's test fills `msg` with the HTTP error or "doesn't look like Moonraker" (`Moonraker.cpp:77-97`). |

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

# One live chat against the real P1S, 2026-11-01

Code under test: `claude/festive-lederberg-693438` (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) plus the
scenario on `claude/printer-live-p1s`. Provider anthropic, model `claude-sonnet-5-5` as read
from the run's app config; the app's log does not record the model name in a request or
response, so that config line is the evidence. Printer: Bambu Lab P1S at 192.168.0.198,
cloud mode, not changed. Ran once, 09:01:48 to 09:02:46 PST.

## Verdict

The model told the truth about the printer and what to do. After the app's note it said the
P1S was found at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, that it cannot connect as it is, that
LAN Only is turned on in the printer's network settings, and that connecting is optional.
It never said there is no printer on the network and gave no menu path.

Things to know:

- At +25 s, 6 seconds before the printer was heard, it said "The app didn't find your P1S on
  the network" after the app's 15-second note. True of what had been observed, but it does
  not say the search is still running, and it asked the person to go and look at the printer.
- It repeated the app's sentence that "the printer can prepare prints without a connection".
  The printer does not prepare prints; the app does. The wording comes from `kPersonsChoice` in
  PrinterConversation.cpp, so the model is faithful to a misleading line. "Network settings" also
  comes from the app's tool description; nobody checked it on the printer in this run.
- It never called `printer_connect`, so no model read the new refusal text in this run.
- The model did not ask for the address; the scenario volunteered it at +37 s.

## Checks

Five of six word and outcome checks passed. `live_p1s_words_invent_no_menu_path` failed on a false
positive: my word list had " menu" and the model said "Connect… in its menu on Home", a real app
menu named in printerInstructions.ts. The list was then narrowed; that narrowing has only been
compiled and checked against this saved transcript, since no second live chat is allowed.

## The first no-model check missed the printer

Before the chat I ran the free `--printer-network-check` twice with this new binary. The first run,
about 08:57, heard nothing for 120 seconds while reporting search state `listening` and failed. A
plain Python listener at 09:00 heard three announcements in 45 seconds. The second run, just after,
heard the printer at 25 s and passed. Cause unknown. My hypothesis, unverified: macOS Local Network
permission on a new executable's first run.

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].

---
name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
description: "2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn"
metadata:

---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a
**Fake A1 mini** printer, connects it to the fake and selects it before it
prints `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY`. Edits to the conf would not survive: the
fixture rewrites it at startup.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |
| `send_fails` | `true` makes the next print or storage upload fail as an upload failure (read at the moment of Send), so OrcaSlicer's send dialog shows its error and reports no success |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## A real printer, no model

The printer tools are not exposed over MCP, so `probe.call` cannot reach them.
`shell_integration_harness --printer-network-check <dir> <address> <version>`
drives them with a scripted stand-in for the model, on Bambu's real plug-in:
copy `plugins/` from a data folder that has it into `<dir>` first, and pass the
version in its `libbambu_networking_<version>.dylib` name. It expects a P1S in
cloud mode at `<address>`, prints each tool result and note as
`HARNESS NETWORK` lines, and sends the printer nothing. `--simulate-announce` after
the version hands the app that announcement itself 25 seconds in, for when no
printer is on; it tests everything after the plug-in, not the plug-in. Printers announce on UDP
2021. While another program holds that port the plug-in hears nothing, and
`printer_connection_status` reports `port_taken`, so quit whatever
`lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` names first. The plug-in takes the port only as the app
starts, so once that program lets go the status reports `not_listening` until a
restart. Holding the port from a small script is how to test both states.

## Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

## Agent id

Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

The bridge still has its own code that strips the field, because the bridge also forwards catalogs from a live app of another version. These adjustments are deliberate, for compatibility. They are not conflicting definitions of the same tool.

### Image results

Three read tools in the candidate catalog return a picture: `project_attachment_read` (a reference image), `view_render` (the prepared or sliced scene), and `printer_camera_snapshot`. The result that the registry produces holds the encoded image and a structured block that describes it (dimensions, camera or layer range, capture time). Each adapter then presents that one result in its own format:

- MCP: an `image` content block next to the text and the structured result. `2025-03-26` gets the same block, because image content is older than structured content.
- OpenAI: the text and the structured block are the function result. The image is appended as an image input in the continuation, because a function result can only be text.

The two adapters present the same result in different formats. The tool itself does not behave differently. Both projections must be tested before the first tool that returns an image ships. Limit every image to 1280 pixels on the long edge and to 2 MB, so that one frame never takes up most of the context window. Never return an image the user has not allowed. A camera frame requires the privacy grant in Printer Configuration. Without it, the call fails with `camera_disabled`.

## Errors should teach the next valid call

When an invalid state is expected, handle it with ordinary control flow and return a structured error. Do not throw an exception. An error should say what the problem is and include only the data the Agent needs to correct the call.

An error is judged by four things, in this order:

1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.
4. **A broken invariant is not reported to the model.** A state the code guarantees cannot happen (a tool with no handler, a coordinator without the product state every app host gives it, a checked id that does not parse) throws, so it reaches Sentry.

Every code a tool can fail with is listed in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`, and `ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail` throws on any other. The in-app agent and MCP clients read the same codes: the MCP adapter passes them through unchanged. Each code stands for one next step:

input.description: Read the stewardship rules on seams and required evidence

result.output:
**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.
**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

An error is judged by four things, in this order:

1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.

# Tool result inventory: slice, export, print and inspect tools

Read from the worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures` at commit 5f3bd2e59a, code only; nothing was built or run. Paths are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this commit.

Vocabulary: a "collapse" is two or more states the app can tell apart at the moment it answers, which the model receives as the same result. Causes are numbered as in the earlier analysis: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event; (2) a filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason; (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined; (4) a generic error was used for a common, distinguishable state. Two new causes came up and are named where they apply: (5) an I/O result is not checked; (6) the result is written before the work happens.

Shared plumbing that every table relies on:

- `workspace_error_code()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83) maps `WorkspaceError` kinds one to one onto codes: NotFound and InvalidId to `not_found`, StaleId and StaleSettings to `stale_workspace`, Busy to `busy`, NeedsStep to `needs_step`, Refused to `refused`, Failed to `failed`, WorkspaceUnavailable to `workspace_unavailable`, InvalidArgument to `invalid_arguments`, FeatureExpired to `feature_expired`. The message is the adapter's own text, so the collapses below are the adapter's, not the mapping's.
- `targets_sliced()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1054-1069) says whether every plate named (all plates when none is named) has `sliced == true`, and copies the first `slice_failure` it meets into `failure`. It starts from `sliced = !snapshot.plates.empty()`, so a plateId that matches no plate leaves `sliced` true.
- `WorkspacePlate::sliced` is `PartPlate::is_slice_result_valid()` read on every snapshot (Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1093); `slicing.running` is `Plater::is_background_process_slicing()`, which is the app-wide `p->m_is_slicing` flag (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:18402-18405). There is one slicing process for the whole app.
- `slice_failure` on a plate is the fork's own record (`m_slice_failures`), written by `record_slice_failure()` (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:977-1004) when OrcaSlicer calls the fork's `report_slice_declined()` hook or when a run ends with `event.error()`. The text comes from the print-issue monitor's first Blocker (`PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp:90-111`) or falls back to `"The app did not start slicing this plate."` (refused) or `"The slice stopped with an error."` (failed). The record is erased when the plate becomes sliced (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935) and when a run starts on the current plate (948-950), and hidden from the snapshot while that plate is slicing (1115-1116).
- `report_slice_declined()` is called from three of OrcaSlicer's exits in `Plater::reslice()` and `Plater::start_next_slice()` (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16070, 16116, 16262). Two other early returns in `reslice()` call nothing: the gizmo-in-editing-mode return (16076-16078) and the "could not stop UI job within 10000 ms" return (16082-16087). The "background process in idle state, use previous result" branch (16153-16165) also calls nothing; it sets the plate valid when it has printable instances and invalid when it has none.

Read from the worktree `.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures` at commit 5f3bd2e59a, code only; nothing was built or run. Paths are relative to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this commit.

Vocabulary: a "collapse" is two or more states the app can tell apart at the moment it answers, which the model receives as the same result. Causes are numbered as in the earlier analysis: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event; (2) a filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason; (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined; (4) a generic error was used for a common, distinguishable state. Two new causes came up and are named where they apply: (5) an I/O result is not checked; (6) the result is written before the work happens.

Shared plumbing that every table relies on:

- `workspace_error_code()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:62-83) maps `WorkspaceError` kinds one to one onto codes: NotFound and InvalidId to `not_found`, StaleId and StaleSettings to `stale_workspace`, Busy to `busy`, NeedsStep to `needs_step`, Refused to `refused`, Failed to `failed`, WorkspaceUnavailable to `workspace_unavailable`, InvalidArgument to `invalid_arguments`, FeatureExpired to `feature_expired`. The message is the adapter's own text, so the collapses below are the adapter's, not the mapping's.
- `targets_sliced()` (Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1054-1069) says whether every plate named (all plates when none is named) has `sliced == true`, and copies the first `slice_failure` it meets into `failure`. It starts from `sliced = !snapshot.plates.empty()`, so a plateId that matches no plate leaves `sliced` true.
- `WorkspacePlate::sliced` is `PartPlate::is_slice_result_valid()` read on every snapshot (Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1093); `slicing.running` is `Plater::is_background_process_slicing()`, which is the app-wide `p->m_is_slicing` flag (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:18402-18405). There is one slicing process for the whole app.
- `slice_failure` on a plate is the fork's own record (`m_slice_failures`), written by `record_slice_failure()` (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:977-1004) when OrcaSlicer calls the fork's `report_slice_declined()` hook or when a run ends with `event.error()`. The text comes from the print-issue monitor's first Blocker (`PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp:90-111`) or falls back to `"The app did not start slicing this plate."` (refused) or `"The slice stopped with an error."` (failed). The record is erased when the plate becomes sliced (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:935) and when a run starts on the current plate (948-950), and hidden from the snapshot while that plate is slicing (1115-1116).
- `report_slice_declined()` is called from three of OrcaSlicer's exits in `Plater::reslice()` and `Plater::start_next_slice()` (src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16070, 16116, 16262). Two other early returns in `reslice()` call nothing: the gizmo-in-editing-mode return (16076-16078) and the "could not stop UI job within 10000 ms" return (16082-16087). The "background process in idle state, use previous result" branch (16153-16165) also calls nothing; it sets the plate valid when it has printable instances and invalid when it has none.

## Collapses by cause

Cause (1), fork reads leftover state instead of the event:
- `slice_start`'s `started` and `alreadySliced` are read from `slicing.running` and `is_slice_result_valid()` after the posted event returns. Two of OrcaSlicer's silent exits in `reslice()` (gizmo editing, UI job not stopped) and the idle branch have no `report_slice_declined()` hook, so they produce the generic refusal or a wrong `alreadySliced`. The live anomaly (sliced plate answered "refused", then `sliced: false`) sits here; its writer is unverified.
- `export_file`, `slice_inspect`, `slice_report` read the app-wide `is_background_process_slicing()` and refuse a valid plate while another plate slices.
- A cancelled run records nothing (`on_process_completed` keys on `event.error()`), so cancel, never sliced and "invalidated, cause unknown" collapse in the slicing section and in `activity_cancel`.
- A run start erases the plate's recorded failure (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:948-950); a cancelled retry therefore loses the reason the model had.

Cause (2), a filter drops the reason:
- `print_dialog_open` fills `failure` and drops it (confirmed (9)).
- `slice_report` with `valid: false` and no record does not say which of never / stale / running it is, although the snapshot has `estimateStatus`.
- `activity_cancel` uses one sentence for four endings of the tools' run, and `not_found` for a handle the tools issued and then superseded.
- `slicing.plates[].sliceFailure` is the short form (no `code`, `objectName`, `sequence`); only `slice_report` has the full one.
- `sliceWarnings` absent means both "none" and "never read while active" for a non-active plate.
- `slice_report` leaves a section out when the check could not run, same as when it was not asked.

Cause (3), fakes only produce imagined states: see the test section.

Cause (4), a generic error for a common, distinguishable state:
- `export_file`'s one `needs_step` sentence for never / stale / refused / failed / running (confirmed (4)).
- `slice_inspect`'s bare `{"valid": false}` for the same five (confirmed (7)).
- `slice_start`'s synthesized "The app did not start slicing this plate." whenever no Blocker is in the monitor.
- `export_file` presets: "the preset files exist" for any empty result (probable, unverified).

New cause (5), an I/O result is not checked: `slice_inspect` view gcode opens the file without `is_open()` and answers `valid: true, gcode: ""` (confirmed (7)).

New cause (6), the result is written before the work happens: `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its `CallAfter`; the deferred open can fail silently (`!m_installed`), show the person an error dialog (plate gone, including a plateId that was never in the project), or decline (`print_again` state moved), and no channel carries that back.

Stated in a description (plausibly intended): `busy` for a running slice and that nobody knows whose run it is; `export_file` needing a sliced plate; `slice_report` and `slice_inspect` saying "not sliced"; `slice_report` returning `valid: false` during a run (stated in `slice_start`'s text only); `print_dialog_open`'s `needs_step` and "opens after the call returns"; `activity_cancel` deferring a job's end to the slicing section. Not stated anywhere: every refusal while another plate slices; the wrong `alreadySliced`; the dropped `failure` texts; the gcode-file I/O hole; the nonexistent-plateId success of `print_dialog_open`; cancelled runs leaving no trace; superseded handles reading as `not_found`.

## Test side (cause 3)

Fake: tests/jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp. Tool tests: tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp. (tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp uses `fail_slice_for_testing` at 4642, 4736, 5979 for chat turns, not tool results.)

What the fake can produce:
- Never sliced: the default plate (`sliced: false`).
- Sliced: `set_plate_sliced(id, true)` (1426-1434); `set_plate_warnings_for_testing` also marks sliced (1406-1414).
- Slicing running: `start_slice` (700-738) sets `slicing.running`, `plate`, `percent: 0` and clears the plate's failure; `finish_slice_for_testing(bool)` (1388-1401) ends it with or without a slice; `cancel_slice` (451-457) ends it without one.
- Refused: `refusal` (742) makes `start_slice` record the failure and start nothing (725-728).
- Failed run: `fail_slice_for_testing(failure)` (757-768) ends the run with `kind: Failed` on the plate.
- Stale estimate: `set_plate_estimate_for_testing` (1438-…) can give an unsliced plate a Recomputing or Stale estimate (snapshot drops a Current one at 51-55).
- Warnings after a slice: `warnings_after_slice` (1402).
- Busy, StaleId and NotFound from `start_slice` (702-711).

What the fake cannot produce, or produces differently from the real adapter:
- `inspect_slice` (405-423) ignores `slicing.running`: a sliced plate inspects fine while a run is in flight, where the real adapter answers `valid: false` (OrcaOutputs.cpp:234). The "inspect during a slice" collapse is untestable here.
- `check_export` (425-438) refuses `needs_step` only for `kind == "gcode"` and only when no plate at all is sliced; the real adapter checks the named plate, `sliced_3mf` too, and the running flag. The "export while slicing" and "export of plate A while plate B slices" collapses are unrepresentable, and `sliced_3mf` needs_step is never exercised.
- `slice_report` (1359-1378) does mirror the running flag (app-wide), so the "report of a valid plate while another slices" state is representable but no test asks for it (the fixture has one plate).
- `start_slice` has three outcomes only (refused, all sliced, begins); OrcaSlicer's silent exits (gizmo, UI job, worker busy, no printable instances) and a plate whose valid flag flips during the call are unrepresentable. The live anomaly cannot be written as a fake test.
- `export_file` (440-448) always succeeds once `check_export` passes; copy/write failures, the presets "nothing written" case, and `busy` for the 3D view do not exist.
- `inspect_slice` view gcode returns a fixed string; a missing G-code file does not exist.
- `cancel_slice` returns `stopped = running`; `cancel_slicing()` returning false while the snapshot says running is unrepresentable.
- The print dialog opener in tests (test_tool_coordinator.cpp:2484-2489) answers synchronously; the deferred `CallAfter` failures do not exist.
- A cancelled run leaving no record is representable (`finish_slice_for_testing(false)`) but no test reads the slicing section afterwards and asserts what the model sees.

What the tests exercise, per tool:
- `slice_start`: began / busy / preempt / finished (668-722); refused with Orca's reason, repeated refusal keeping `sequence`, `slice_report` showing the refusal, nothing-to-slice `alreadySliced`, began with chat and MCP notes, handle cleared across projects (2105-2202); `not_found` for a wrong plate (2411). Not exercised: `started: false` with the synthesized generic reason; `alreadySliced` on a mixed set of plates; preempt's effect on the running run.
- `activity_cancel`: stop a running tools' slice, second cancel `cancelled: false`, a person's later run not stopped, `not_found` for an unknown handle (2251-2264). Not exercised: a superseded handle; job cancel states; the four-endings sentence read against what actually ended.
- `export_file`: exists-without-overwrite, overwrite, license in title and result, `sliceWarnings` empty and filled, schema rejections, `not_found` for a wrong plate with `stl` (2266-2321, 2425). Not exercised: `needs_step` "Slice the plate first" at all (grep finds the string only in the fake), any `failed`, `busy`, presets, `stale_workspace` on a changed slice.
- `slice_inspect`: `valid: false` unsliced, layers paging, gcode text (2235-2244); `not_found` (2411). Not exercised: during a run, after a refusal or failure, missing file.
- `slice_report`: `valid: false` unsliced with no summary, summary, findings order and `appliesWhen`, material, `valid: false` during a run (724-842); the refusal's `sliceFailure` (2140-2145); region checks (2013). Not exercised: `sliceFailure.kind: "failed"` at the tool level; a valid plate while another plate slices; absent sections when a check cannot run.
- `print_dialog_open`: `needs_step` for an unsliced plate, opened for a sliced one, gcode refused by the host, argument validation (2477-2515). Not exercised: a nonexistent `plateId` (not in the 2411 list); `no_printer`; `not_found`/ambiguous gcode; any deferred-open failure.
- `workspace_inspect`: default sections present (650-666); slicing section during and after a run (690-722); printer section (877); auto-orient jobs (1408). Not exercised: slicing section after a cancel, after a failed run, with `sliceFailure` next to `estimateStatus`; `activities`; `project`; `objects` as a section (objects_section_result is tested through other tools).

Worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/tool-silent-failures`, commit 5f3bd2e59a. Read only; nothing built or run. All paths below are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `tests/` or `src/`.

Abbreviations: Coord = `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`; Adapter = `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`; Registry = `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`; Results = `Agent/ToolResults.cpp`.

Causes used in the "Collapse?" column: (1) fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened; (2) a filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason; (3) tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined; (4) a generic error was used for a state that is common and distinguishable; (5, new) a handler throws, so the call never gets a result at all.

# Tool result inventory: what the app can tell apart, and what the model reads

Written 2026-11-01, from the code at `5f3bd2e59a` (`jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4` plus the Bambu connection fix). It answers one question for every tool the model can call:

**Does every state the app can tell apart at the moment it answers map to a result the model can tell apart?**

Where two states the app distinguishes produce the same result (the same code and message, an empty list, a bare `valid: false`, or a success that says nothing), the row is a **collapse**. The rule these rows are held to is in the tool guide, ["A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result"](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#a-reason-travels-with-every-refusal-and-every-empty-result), and in the header of `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`.

## How to use this document

- **Adding or changing a tool:** list its states here first, one row each, and say what the result carries for each. A tool is not done while a row collapses. The guard for a tool is a state table test that arranges each row and asserts the results differ (`tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` under the `[states]` tag, `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", and the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`).
- **Reading a row:** "Where" is the code that distinguishes the state at `5f3bd2e59a` (paths under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`). "Result" quotes what the model reads. "Cause" is one of the numbered causes below. "Status" says whether the collapse is open, fixed, or accepted.
- **Reproduction before a fix:** a collapse is fixed only once it has been reproduced in the real app or the real harness. The status column says how each one was. Kenneth's rule: no fix for a failure not reproduced; a fake taught to fail is not a reproduction on its own.

## Why these collapses exist: the causes

The tool guide governs what the model is told and how a tool is shaped. These collapses are on the app's side, in the code that reads OrcaSlicer's state and turns it into a result. Six causes account for every row below; the first four were named before this inventory, the last two were found while writing it.

1. **Fork code reads OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event that happened.** `OrcaPrinterBackend` reported a failed Bambu connection as "The selected printer changed" because upstream's handler clears the selection on failure; the slice tools read the app-wide "is slicing" flag instead of which plate's run it is.
2. **A filter encodes a product decision and drops the reason.** Connection candidates of another model, hidden presets, a key that belongs to another scope: the loop that drops them keeps no record, and the model reads an empty list.
3. **Tests and fakes only produce the states their author imagined.** The Bambu fake never sent `ConnectStatusFailed`; the harness check for a failed connection simulated a selection change instead; the fake workspace has no hidden presets, no empty render, no refused host.
4. **A generic error was used for states that are common and that the app distinguishes.** Kenneth's 2026-10-15 rule gives one generic error to failures that are rare and that the app cannot tell apart. Applied to never sliced, refused, failed and slicing now, which the snapshot tells apart, it became cause 4.
5. **A result is written before the work happens, or without checking the work's outcome.** `print_dialog_open` answers `opened: true` before its deferred open; `slice_inspect` reads a G-code file without checking that it opened.
6. **A dialog or a throw outside any channel.** OrcaSlicer shows the person a dialog in the middle of a tool call that no scope answers, or a handler throws and the activity never gets a result at all.
