### workspace_inspect

Summary, slicing, printer, project, objects, plan, activities, history. The sections report their sources' states well: `estimateStatus` separates never sliced from stale, `slicing.running` with `plateId` and `percent` says what runs, `sliceFailure` and `sliceWarnings` ride on each plate. Open collapses, all minor: the default summary's `sliced` alone hides a run in progress (stated by the section design); `sliceFailure` here is the short form without `code`, `objectName` or `sequence`; a `sliceWarnings` absent on a non-active plate means both none and never read; a cancelled run leaves no trace anywhere (cause 1); `observed` absent covers no device bound, nothing found and discovery not possible (cause 2); `plan` empty and no plan look the same; `printHistory`, which `print_dialog_open`'s description points at, exists only in the chat's request context and in no section.

## Project, object, region and picture tools

### project_open, object_import, object_import_file

Path, extension, `openedBefore` (with whether the file changed), the projects store being unreadable, and the release of the open project being cancelled each have their own code and sentence. OrcaSlicer's dialogs, notifications and `show_error` texts during the load travel in `report.messages` with the answer the app gave. Collapses, open, cause 4: "The app did not open that file" and "The app did not import that file" carry no reason when Orca was silent; a model file that loaded nothing still reports `projectOpened: true` because the empty project was made first; an empty file is reported as "The model file does not exist".

### project_delete_items

Every id, part, instance and plate case has its own sentence. Open: a dialog Orca raises mid-delete is logged, not returned (cause 1 and 6); a region removal failing after the deletions ran does not say so (cause 4, rare).

### plate_layout

Each refusal (cut object, disabled object, editing tool open, plate limit, slicing, busy worker, unknown plate type) is its own sentence. Open: a no-op row looks like an applied row (plausibly intended); moving an object whose copies sit on different plates shifts every copy by the first copy's delta and reports one `plateIds` list (cause 2); an arrange that `failed` carries no reason while Orca shows the person "Arrange failed" and "ignored the following objects" (cause 1 and 2).

### object_place

Open: two sizing facets, two orientation facets or no facet at all get the bare contract sentence (cause 4); a `faceDown` handle of another object, malformed, with a bad volume or plane, or a hole handle where a face is wanted, all read "is not a face of this object" (cause 4); a `unitsFix` discards the dialog answers it collected and assumes the last object is the converted one (cause 1; the wrong-id part unverified); a zero-extent `scaleTo` fails after a units fix already ran (cause 4, rare).

### object_divide_preview, object_divide

Open: plane and shells together get the bare contract sentence (cause 4); a plane that crosses the bounding box but misses the mesh reports a one-piece success with a new id (cause 1, unverified); shells to objects where Orca splits nothing shows the person "The selected object couldn't be split." and reports a one-piece success naming the last object (cause 1 and 6, unverified); the auto-drop question is shown to the person mid-call (cause 6, unverified).

### object_merge

Open: "The app cannot merge these objects" when the live cause after the adapter's own checks is an unregistered selection or SLA (cause 1); the count check may report a successful merge of multi-copy objects as `failed` (unverified).

### object_repair

Reports every reason and its partial progress ("Already changed by this call, and not undone: its painted supports ... were removed; j of its n open parts were repaired."). No collapse. The model for the rest.

### region_annotate

Argument refusals are exemplary ("<handle> is a hole handle, not a face handle; use the handles listed under features holes"). Open: a new direction region whose cone contains no facet reads "No facet of X matches that face any more" with code `stale_workspace`, which is neither stale nor a face and sends the model to re-read (cause 4, common); a box or cylinder volume that intersects no part is a success (cause 2); a mid-apply failure after replaced regions were removed does not say so (cause 4, rare); five structural handle problems read "is not a feature of <name>" (cause 4, mild).

### object_analyze

Open, all cause 2 unless said: `mesh.partList` caps at 16 with no `truncated` flag, so JusPrin's own region volumes can vanish from the list; a plane whose border could not be walked is dropped silently; `fit.overlaps` checks the first instance's plate only; `measurement: {}` says nothing about which quantities are undefined; `bindingLost` is never computed for box, cylinder, direction and object regions (cause 3); a region whose object cannot be matched shows both flags true and no `objectId`; a `faceDown` candidate that is a hole or another object's handle reads "is not a face of this object" (cause 4). `parts` counts shells while `partList` lists volumes: a naming trap, not a collapse.

### project_attachment_read, skill_read

Open, minor: a refused folder or a path traversal reads "no attachment" (plausibly intended); a corrupt image and one too large after re-encoding share "The app could not read that picture" (cause 4). `skill_read` has no collapse.

### view_render

"The app rendered nothing" is unreachable: `ThumbnailData::is_valid()` fails only for a zero size, which the adapter clamps away. An empty plate, a plate whose objects are all disabled or partly outside it, an incomplete framebuffer and a missing shader all return a valid blank PNG as success, while OrcaSlicer counted the visible volumes and logged the failure (`src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp:6194-6220, 6495`). Cause 1; open; not stated. An object partly off the plate is omitted from the picture, which is exactly the object a placement check is about.

and the five printer-chat tools, the states the app can distinguish when it
answers, where in the code it distinguishes them, what the model reads today,
and every place two states read the same. Each collapse carries one of six
causes: reading OrcaSlicer's leftover state instead of the event, a filter
that drops its reason, fakes that only produce imagined states, a generic
error for common states, a result written before the work or without checking
it, and a dialog or throw outside any channel. The eleven findings are
mapped to their rows; every status is open at this commit.

A new tool adds its rows here before it ships, and a row that collapses is
what the state-table guards in tests/agent assert against.
EOF

State the rule a tool result is held to: a reason travels with every refusal

The tool error contract (Agent/ToolErrors.hpp and the guide's "Errors should
teach the next valid call") governs the code a failure carries and the next
step it names. It said nothing about the other half of a result: what it lets
the model tell apart. The sweep of 2026-11-01 found eleven tools answering
with a generic sentence, an empty list or a bare valid: false for states the
app distinguishes.

The rule, in both places: every state the app can tell apart at the moment it
answers maps to a result the model can tell apart. A refusal carries the
reason from the event the app read, not from what the event left behind; an
empty list says why it is empty when the app dropped something it knew of;
sibling tools say the same thing about the same state in the same fields; a
generic error is allowed only for a failure that is rare and that the app
itself cannot distinguish; fakes produce every state the real owner reports.

The fourth point keeps Kenneth's rule of 2026-10-15 as it was made: rare,
speculative failures get one generic error with no per-cause handling. That
rule is about failures the app has nothing more to say about, and it never
licensed one message for states the app does tell apart. The guide says so
next to the rule, so the two are read together.
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -2
